newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's says affirms Nippon Credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says affirms Nippon Credit ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday it had affirmed Nippon Credit Bank Ltd's (NCB) deposit, financial strength and debt ratings.

The credit research firm said in a statement that it had affirmed the Japanese long-term credit bank's Ba1 senior debt rating, Baa3/P-3 deposit ratings and E financial strength ratings. The rating outlook remains negative, it added.
The affirmation was in response to NCB's restructuring plans announced on April 1, it said.
"Despite significant restructuring plans, the bank's financial fundamentals remain weak and it may ultimately require additional outside assistance," Moody's said.
"The bank's asset quality trend entails a degree of uncertainty, given its significant commercial real estate concentration," it added.
Moody's said that of particular concern to the rating agency is the bank's ability to re-establish access to the long-term bank debenture market at a reasonable cost.
Such access is crucial for NCB to remain viable on a stand-alone basis, it said.
"New capital provided by the authorities and Japanese financial firms may prove to be inadequate, in and of itself, to address the bank's problems," Moody's said.
It said NCB's recent discussions with Bankers Trust did not contain elements that were likely to result in quick improvements in its financial fundamentals.

The Japanese authorities' continuing use of a "case-by-case" approach to bank resolutions created uncertainty for investors, particularly because some of the cases involve recapitalisation and losses to creditors.
Moody's said the NCB case was the first in which Japanese authorities had allowed one of the 20 major Japanese banks to default on certain of its debt obligations such as subordinated loans.
"Without explicit protection, certain creditor classes may be exposed to greater risks," it added.
In this context, Moody's said it made a rating differentiation between deposits and senior debt.
